caption: The drawing is a black-and-white illustration of a clock face contained within a rectangular border. The main circular clock face features large Roman numerals from I to XII to indicate the hours, surrounded by an outer ring of Arabic numerals in intervals of five, going from 5 to 60, to indicate the minutes. There are two clock hands, one longer and one shorter, both ornately decorated. Above the center of the clock face is a semicircular section, within which is an illustration of an eagle perched atop a ribboned decorative element. The words "UT HORA SIC VITA TRANSIT" are inscribed in a curved arc above the eagle. There are elaborate scrollwork decorations at the corners of the main square enclosing the clock face. The central part of the clock face also features decorative elements and contains the text "Benja. Willard" and "Roxbury" in a cursive script, along with a small inner dial labeled "No 1793" and “Patented.” The entire illustration is composed of dark ink lines and shading on an off-white background. The artist's name, "N. Tould," is written in small script in the lower left margin outside the main bordered area.
title: Clock
